t:
(a) 
The Secretary, for the purposes of this title, shall have the power to determine and prescribe the standards of adequate farm housing and other buildings, by farms or localities, taking into consideration, among other factors, the type of housing which will provide decent, safe, and sanitary dwelling for the needs of the family using the housing, the type and character of the farming operations to be conducted, and the size and earning capacity of the land.
 
    (b) 
The Secretary may require any recipient of a loan or grant to agree that the availability of improvements constructed or repaired with the proceeds of the loan or grant under this title shall not be a justification for directly or indirectly changing the terms or conditions of the lease or occupancy agreement with the occupants of such farms to the latter's disadvantage without the approval of the Secretary.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the power to "determine and prescribe the standards" amounts to rulemaking, which would count as participation. But the text does not say "by regulation" or require any comment period, hearing, advisory body, or consultation with anyone outside the federal government; the Secretary decides alone based on listed factors. Subsection (b) only imposes a condition on loan or grant recipients, which is a term of a benefit rather than outside involvement in a federal decision.
fable.s: The Secretary, for the purposes of this title, shall have the power to determine and prescribe the standards of adequate farm housing and other buildings, by farms or localities

qwen_block.w: This section grants the Secretary the authority to determine standards and requires recipients of loans or grants to agree to certain conditions. It does not require the Secretary to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making these determinations. The 'taking into consideration' clause refers to factual factors (housing type, farming operations), not to a process of engaging with external stakeholders. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary, for the purposes of this title, shall have the power to determine and prescribe the standards of adequate farm housing and other buildings, by farms or localities, taking into consideration, among other factors, the type of housing which will provide decent, safe, and sanitary dwelling for the needs of the family using the housing, the type and character of the farming operations to be conducted, and the size and earning capacity of the land.

opus.w: Subsection (a) lets the Secretary prescribe general standards for farm housing and other buildings, which in practice means rulemaking, and the DEFINITION and Example 6 treat regulatory authority as participation. Subsection (b) does not count, because agreements with loan or grant recipients are part of applying for benefits. The opposite reading has some force because the statute never explicitly says "by regulation", so the standards might be set without any public process.
opus.s: The Secretary, for the purposes of this title, shall have the power to determine and prescribe the standards of adequate farm housing and other buildings, by farms or localities
opus.b:
I labelled this "Yes", but only narrowly (confidence 0.55).

1. **The tempting reading, and why it fails.** It is tempting to say "No": no outside party is named, and subsection (b) is about agreements with loan or grant recipients, which counts as applying for benefits and is not participation. That reading misses subsection (a). It lets the Secretary "determine and prescribe the standards" for farm housing "by farms or localities". These are general standards, and federal agencies normally set such standards through rulemaking with public notice and comment. The DEFINITION counts any requirement of rulemaking as participation, and Example 6 counts even optional regulatory authority.

2. **Why the call is close.** The text never says "regulation" or "rulemaking". The Secretary could set the standards through internal guidance with no public process.

qwen_chat.w: The section grants the Secretary unilateral authority to determine standards without requiring consultation with outside parties. While it mentions considering factors like family needs, it does not mandate a process for obtaining input from those families or the public. The requirement for recipients to get approval for lease changes is a condition of a loan or grant, which the definition explicitly excludes from participation.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary, for the purposes of this title, shall have the power to determine and prescribe the standards of adequate farm housing and other buildings, by farms or localities, taking into consideration, among other factors, the type of housing which will provide decent, safe, and sanitary dwelling for the needs of the family using the housing, the type and character of the farming operations to be conducted, and the size and earning capacity of the land.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretary's power to "determine and prescribe standards" implies a process of gathering input from farmers or local communities, or that the requirement for recipients to get approval for lease changes involves consultation. However, the text itself does not mandate any consultation, hearing, or comment period with outside parties. The Secretary's determination is unilateral, and the recipient's obligation is to obtain approval, which is an administrative condition of a grant/loan, not a participatory decision-making process involving the public or outside entities in the formulation of policy. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants.
